titleEn: Horror films exploit how human vision works to deliver movies’ best scares
titleZh: 恐怖片如何利用人类视觉，制造令人难忘的惊吓
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: This article contains spoilers from popular horror movies and shows.
paragraphs.zh: 这篇文章包含从流行的恐怖电影和节目剧透。

paragraphs.en: Imagine you’re in the movie theater watching 2018’s “Hereditary.” During one of the film’s most unsettling sequences, the main character, Peter, wakes up in bed disoriented. As he sits up, you hear a couple of gasps from others in the audience. The camera stays locked on Peter as he moves through his house and enters the dim living room.
paragraphs.zh: 想象一下，你在电影院里观看2018年的《遗传》（Hereditary）。在这部电影最令人不安的一幕中，主角彼得在床上醒来，迷失了方向。当他坐起来时，你听到观众中其他人的喘息声。当彼得穿过他的房子，进入昏暗的客厅时，镜头一直锁定在他身上。

paragraphs.en: You hear it again: more gasps. The lighting is low, a droning score builds tension, and your heart rate climbs. The people around you continue to audibly react. You haven’t seen anything scary yet, so what is everyone else responding to?
paragraphs.zh: 你又听到了：更多的喘息声。灯光很暗，嗡嗡作响的配乐让人紧张，你的心跳加速。你周围的人继续听到你的反应。你还没有看到任何可怕的东西，那么其他人的反应是什么呢？

paragraphs.en: The camera slowly pulls back, and then you see her: Annie, Peter’s possessed mother, crouched on the ceiling in an unnatural way.
paragraphs.zh: 镜头慢慢地向后拉，然后你看到了她：安妮，彼得被附身的母亲，以一种不自然的方式蹲在天花板上。

paragraphs.en: Watch the scene again and you might notice that Annie was in the shadows on the ceiling the whole time, following Peter through the house.
paragraphs.zh: 再看一遍这个场景，你可能会注意到安妮一直在天花板上的阴影里，跟着彼得穿过房子。

paragraphs.en: How could you have missed a human being on the ceiling, in plain view?
paragraphs.zh: 你怎么能错过一个人在天花板上，在平原的看法？

paragraphs.en: As a cognitive psychologist who studies visual perception, I’ve noticed that horror movies often exploit the gap between what’s in front of your eyes and what you consciously see. Directors and cinematographers act like folk cognitive psychologists, intuitively drawing your attention exactly where it needs to be to create a scare.
paragraphs.zh: 作为一名研究视觉感知的认知心理学家，我注意到恐怖电影经常利用你眼前的东西和你有意识地看到的东西之间的差距。导演和摄影师就像民间认知心理学家一样，直觉地把你的注意力吸引到需要制造恐慌的地方。

paragraphs.en: Directing your attention
paragraphs.zh: 引导你的注意力

paragraphs.en: Horror movie fans have pointed out numerous examples of spooky figures and other unnoticed details in the background of scenes.
paragraphs.zh: 恐怖电影迷们指出了许多场景背景中幽灵般的人物和其他不被注意的细节。

paragraphs.en: These blind spots exist because your visual system can’t process everything in a scene at once. You extract detailed information only from wherever your attention is directed. Anything outside the spotlight of your attention may go unnoticed, no matter how strange.
paragraphs.zh: 这些盲点的存在是因为你的视觉系统不能同时处理场景中的所有内容。你只能从你的注意力所指向的地方提取详细信息。任何在你注意力聚光灯之外的东西都可能被忽视，无论多么奇怪。

paragraphs.en: Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice something in plain view because your attention is engaged elsewhere; it’s the phenomenon behind the infamous invisible gorilla experiment, in which about half of participants busy counting basketball passes failed to notice a person in a gorilla suit strolling through the middle of the game.
paragraphs.zh: 无意视盲是指你的注意力被其他地方吸引而没有注意到明显的东西;这是臭名昭著的隐形大猩猩实验背后的现象，在这个实验中，大约一半的参与者忙碌忙于计算篮球传球，没有注意到一个穿着大猩猩服装的人在比赛中间漫步。

paragraphs.en: Horror leans on inattentional blindness frequently, from the ghost boy in “Insidious” to the background ghosts scattered through Netflix’s “The Haunting of Hill House.” Something is plainly visible, though you often don’t notice it until a rewatch, and this delayed discovery can make the scene even creepier.
paragraphs.zh: 恐怖片常常依赖于无意视盲，从《潜伏》（Insidious）中的幽灵男孩，到Netflix的《山屋惊魂》（The Haunting of Hill House）中散落的背景幽灵。有些东西是显而易见的，尽管你通常要到重看时才注意到，而这种延迟的发现会让场景变得更加毛骨悚然。

paragraphs.en: A related effect, change blindness, is the failure to notice something changing right in front of you. The difference can be as simple as a shirt color, or something drastic like the possessed girl Janet in “The Conjuring 2” morphing into an old man during her interview with Ed Warren. The camera stays on Ed while Janet sits slightly blurred in the background, making the transformation easy to miss until she abruptly changes back.
paragraphs.zh: 与此相关的一种效应是“变化盲视”，即无法注意到你眼前的事物发生了变化。这种变化可能很简单，比如衬衫的颜色，也可能是一些非常严重的变化，比如《招魂2》中被附身的女孩珍妮特在采访艾德·沃伦时变成了一个老人。镜头一直对准艾德，而珍妮特坐在背景中，稍微有些模糊。所以很容易忽略她的变化直到她突然变回来

paragraphs.en: Directors also steer your attention to set up a scare, pulling your focus away from something creepy, or putting it in exactly the right spot just before a jump scare.
paragraphs.zh: 导演也会引导你的注意力来设置一个惊吓，把你的注意力从一些令人毛骨悚然的东西上移开，或者在一个跳跃惊吓之前把它放在正确的位置。

paragraphs.en: Eyeline match is a perfect example of this strategy. In “The Conjuring,” a girl sits up in bed, her fearful eyes fixed upward. The film cuts to reveal she’s staring at the ghost Bathsheba, crouched atop a wardrobe.
paragraphs.zh: 眼线匹配是这种策略的一个完美例子。在《招魂》中，一个女孩从床上坐起来，她恐惧的眼睛向上凝视。电影剪辑显示她盯着蜷缩在衣柜上的幽灵阿杜谢芭。

paragraphs.en: This editing technique works because it’s similar to something your visual system does: When someone near you looks sharply in one direction, your eyes follow automatically. Psychologists call this tendency gaze cueing, a reliable effect in attention research. Editing just mimics the real-life version to create tension, which resolves the moment you finally see what the character sees.
paragraphs.zh: 这种编辑技术之所以有效，是因为它类似于你的视觉系统：当你身边的人朝一个方向看时，你的眼睛会自动跟随。心理学家称这种倾向为凝视暗示，这是注意力研究中的一种可靠效应。编辑只是模仿现实生活中的版本，以制造紧张感，从而解决你最终看到角色所看到的那一刻。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes directors do the opposite, giving your attention nothing to follow at all. The opening sequence of “It Follows” is a wide shot of a panicked girl running in and out of her house. With no eyeline or cut to guide you, the wide framing forces you into visual search, scanning corner to corner for a danger that may not even be there yet. Will something appear in a window? Follow her out the door? The uncertainty and the search build the tension.
paragraphs.zh: 有时候，导演的做法恰恰相反，让你的注意力根本无从追踪。《跟随》的开场镜头是一个惊慌失措的女孩跑进跑出她的房子的广角镜头。没有视线或镜头来引导你，宽阔的框架迫使你进行视觉搜索，一个角落一个角落地扫描，寻找可能还没有出现的危险。会有什么东西出现在窗户里吗？跟着她出门吗？不确定性和探索造成了紧张。

paragraphs.en: The split between detecting and identifying
paragraphs.zh: 检测和识别之间的分离

paragraphs.en: Your visual field isn’t equally good at everything: Some parts of your visual system perform the initial detection, others identify what was detected. For example, the fovea, a tiny pit in the retina that processes the spot you’re looking directly at, contains photoreceptors called cones that process fine detail and color.
paragraphs.zh: 你的视野并不是在所有事情上都一样好：你的视觉系统的一些部分执行最初的检测，其他部分识别检测到的东西。例如，中央凹，视网膜上的一个小坑，处理你直视的斑点，包含被称为视锥细胞的光感受器，处理细节和颜色。

paragraphs.en: Beyond that central spot is your peripheral vision, dominated by photoreceptors called rods that are sensitive to motion and low light rather than detail. In a sense, your peripheral vision is set up to help you quickly answer the question “Did something just move?”
paragraphs.zh: 在中心点之外是你的周边视觉，由称为视杆细胞的感光细胞控制，它们对运动和弱光敏感，而不是细节。从某种意义上说，你的周边视觉是为了帮助你快速回答“刚才有什么东西在动吗？”

paragraphs.en: When there’s motion at the edge of your vision, your peripheral system detects it almost instantly. Your eyes make a saccade – a rapid eye movement – to place the fovea onto the target to identify it. That gap between detecting and identifying can create a feeling of unease because something registered, something is there, but you can’t yet say what.
paragraphs.zh: 当你的视觉边缘有运动时，你的周边系统几乎会立即察觉到。你的眼睛会进行扫视--一种快速的眼球运动--将中央凹置于目标上，以识别它。察觉和识别之间的间隙会产生一种不安的感觉，因为有些东西被记录下来了，有些东西就在那里，但你还说不出是什么。

paragraphs.en: Playing with peripheral vision is almost a trope in horror movies now. Think of any hallway or mirror scene where you’re focused on a character and something moves behind them, grabbing your attention before you can figure out what it is.
paragraphs.zh: 在恐怖电影中，玩弄周边视觉几乎是一个比喻。想想任何走廊或镜子场景，你专注于一个角色，有东西在他们身后移动，在你弄清楚它是什么之前抓住你的注意力。

paragraphs.en: Faces where there are none
paragraphs.zh: 没有面孔

paragraphs.en: Human beings evolved to quickly detect, identify and respond to potential threats, such as moving animals. That’s one reason vision is so sensitive to detecting movement.
paragraphs.zh: 人类进化到可以快速检测、识别和应对潜在威胁，比如移动的动物。这就是视觉对检测运动如此敏感的原因之一。

paragraphs.en: It also explains why people are prone to pareidolia: the human bias toward detecting faces even where none exist. Have you ever seen a face in your curtains or toast? Missing a real face is potentially far costlier than perceiving a fake one, so our brains likely evolved to respond even to patterns that vaguely resemble faces.
paragraphs.zh: 这也解释了为什么人们容易产生幻觉：即使没有面孔，人类也会偏向于发现面孔。你有没有在你的窗帘或吐司上看到过一张脸？错过一张真实的面孔可能比看到一张假面孔要昂贵得多，所以我们的大脑很可能进化到即使是对模糊的面孔模式也会做出反应。

paragraphs.en: “Midsommar” exploits pareidolia directly. As Dani is carried toward the feast after her crowning as May Queen, viewers have noticed a face in the trees. “The Night House” uses a similar trick, where ambiguous object configurations resolve into figures and faces that capture your attention. The 1963 film “The Haunting” does the same with a wall pattern during a particularly creepy scene.
paragraphs.zh: 《仲夏夜之梦》直接利用了幻想症。当丹妮被加冕为五月皇后后被抬着走向宴会时，观众注意到树上有一张脸。《夜屋》使用了类似的技巧，模糊的物体配置分解成吸引你注意力的人物和面孔。1963年的电影《闹鬼》在一个特别令人毛骨悚然的场景中使用了同样的墙壁图案。

paragraphs.en: Directors decide what you get to see and what they leave hidden, from ambiguous shapes to sudden movements to shadowy figures in the background. They seem to understand how your visual system works, and they use this knowledge to create tension in that space between perception and recognition, as your brain tries to determine what, exactly, you’re seeing.
paragraphs.zh: 导演们决定你能看到什么，以及他们隐藏了什么，从模糊的形状到突然的动作，再到背景中的阴影。他们似乎了解你的视觉系统是如何工作的，他们利用这一知识在感知和识别之间的空间中制造紧张，因为你的大脑试图确定你到底看到了什么。
